oneLine: On Saturday 3 October, Bitcoin and Ethereum both rose modestly while most altcoins drifted sideways—the market showed healthy conviction despite regulatory turbulence in the US and EU, with Chainalysis connecting North Korea to the Bitget hack and bankers suing the US banking regulator over crypto trust bank charters.
caveman: On Saturday, Bitcoin (the big one) went up about 0.27%, and Ethereum went up about 0.70%. This is a calm, normal day. Most of the market went up too—almost 63% of all the little coins on Binance went higher. The really big traders are betting things will keep going up. People were buying more aggressively than selling. However, there was big news: people found out that hackers from North Korea stole $387 million from the Bitget exchange back on September 24. Plus, regular banks sued the US government because they're mad that crypto companies can now get special bank charters. Europe is also making new rules about stablecoins (coins that try to stay at one price). One group called NEAR Intents got robbed, but they got all their money back after giving the thief 48 hours to return it. It was a calm day with good signs for the market, but plenty of serious business happening behind the scenes.
priceVolumeSummary: Bitcoin closed at $84,710.60 on Binance, up 0.27% on the day; all five major venues (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Gate) agreed on price within a narrow $14 range. Total daily volume across the five venues topped $8.7 billion, with Binance leading at $3.66 billion.
positioningSummary: Funding rates split sharply: Binance's rate turned negative (−1.47% annualized), signaling caution, while Bybit, Bitget, OKX, and Gate all showed strong bullish funding (3.1–11% annualized), suggesting traders were comfortable holding long positions despite the negative read at the largest venue. Bitcoin open interest on Binance stood at 97,921 coins ($8.29 billion). The top-trader long/short ratio hit 2.05, meaning the largest traders were heavily long—betting on further upside. Taker buy/sell ratio of 1.02 showed slightly more aggressive buying pressure. Market breadth was strong at 62.8% of Binance perpetual pairs up on the day, indicating broad bullish conviction even amid regulatory headlines.
stocksSummary: Saturday is a weekend; US equity markets (S&P 500, Nasdaq), Asian stock markets (Korea KRX, Hong Kong HKEX, China Shanghai/Shenzhen), and commodity futures were all closed. No cash session activity to report.

topThree.headline: Chainalysis traces $387M Bitget hack to North Korean actors, pushing 2026 DPRK crypto theft past $1 billion
topThree.what: Chainalysis published forensic analysis on October 3 linking the September 24 Bitget breach to North Korea-linked threat actors. The firm's AI-assisted investigation identified how $387 million moved across Ethereum (49.7%), XRP (40.8%), Zcash (7.6%), and Tron (1.8%) in under 10 minutes, compressing what would have taken 20+ hours of manual work. This brings 2026's total crypto theft attributed to DPRK-linked groups above $1 billion.

topThree.headline: Independent Community Bankers of America sue US banking regulator over crypto trust bank charters
topThree.what: The ICBA filed suit in US District Court for the District of Columbia on October 2, arguing the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) exceeded its authority by issuing a rule (effective March 2, 2026) that lets non-fiduciary digital-asset companies obtain national trust bank charters. The group contends crypto firms can now bypass obligations (Community Reinvestment Act, FDIC insurance) that bind traditional community banks. The OCC has approved or conditionally approved 21 trust banks, with 13 tied to crypto.

topThree.headline: NEAR Intents recovers full $3.8M stolen in exploit after giving hacker 48-hour ultimatum
topThree.what: NEAR Intents, a cross-chain trading protocol, recovered all $3.8 million drained in an October 1 exploit ahead of the October 4 deadline. The team's ability to identify the exploiter and issue an ultimatum via public channels prompted the thief to return funds in full on October 2. NEAR attributed the initial breach to a bug in its Omni bridge interaction with the smart contract and has since patched the vulnerability.

Regulation and policy.headline: ESMA proposes ending EU custody and transfer services for non-compliant stablecoins
Regulation and policy.what: The European Securities and Markets Authority issued a proposal on October 3 (in its MiCA review response) asking the European Commission to prohibit crypto-asset service providers from offering custody and transfer services for stablecoins that fail MiCA requirements. Currently, ESMA acknowledges such services are not explicitly forbidden, but the proposal would tighten the regime. No implementation date or asset-withdrawal pathway has been set.
Regulation and policy.coins: Stablecoins (generally; USDC and others outside compliance)

Institutional flows and ETFs.headline: Bitcoin ETFs resume net inflows while Ethereum ETFs post outflows for the week
Institutional flows and ETFs.what: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $102.7–103 million in net inflows on October 3, ending a brief outflow period. For the week of September 28–October 2, Bitcoin ETFs saw $82.9 million in net inflows (down sharply from $2.39 billion the prior week, reflecting quarter-end rebalancing on September 30). Ethereum ETFs, by contrast, posted $118 million in net outflows for the same week, with withdrawals on four of five trading days.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Arbitrum pauses new Stylus smart-contract activations over AI-assisted attack risks
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Arbitrum announced a pause on fresh activations of its Stylus WebAssembly programming environment, citing newly identified vulnerability vectors that could be exploited with AI assistance. Existing Stylus programs remain operational. A separate proof-conflict guard can delay unconfirmed withdrawals to Ethereum as an added safeguard.

glossary.definition: A fee paid by traders holding long (bullish) or short (bearish) positions in perpetual futures. Positive rates mean long-side traders pay short-side traders; negative rates are the reverse. High funding rates signal strong bullish conviction; low or negative rates signal caution or bearishness.

The proportion of open long positions (bets the price will rise) compared to short positions (bets the price will fall). A ratio above 1 means more traders are betting up; below 1 means more are betting down.

The percentage of assets in a market that moved up during a period, compared to those that moved down. High breadth (e.g., 63% up) suggests widespread bullish sentiment; low breadth suggests weakness across the board.

The total number of open long and short positions in derivatives (perpetual futures, options) that have not yet been closed. Rising OI suggests increasing leverage and conviction; falling OI suggests traders are closing positions.
The daily or period-over-period increase or decrease in the total open interest. A rise signals new money entering the market; a fall signals liquidation or position-taking off the table.
A measure of aggressive buying vs. selling pressure. Values above 1 mean more aggressive buying (takers initiating long trades); below 1 means more aggressive selling. Values near 1 indicate balance.
The long/short ratio among only the largest traders (whales), excluding retail. This metric isolates what the biggest players are betting and is watched as a leading indicator of price direction.

A type of futures contract (like betting contracts) with no expiration date, allowing traders to hold long or short positions indefinitely. The funding rate ensures prices stay near the spot (current market) price.
A cryptocurrency designed to maintain a fixed price (usually $1) by being backed by a reserve of dollars, other assets, or algorithms. Examples: USDC, USDT, USDP.
The reference price used for perpetual futures contracts, usually a time-weighted average of prices across major exchanges. Used to calculate funding and margin requirements.
